packageRules.description: Pin every NuGet reference to an exact version. A floating x.y.* resolves to whatever is newest at restore time, so a released tag stops restoring once a newer patch raises a dependency floor: v2.3.2 broke that way with NU1605 (#425). Renovate opens a pin PR for any float that is added later.

Microsoft.AspNetCore.TestHost is referenced twice in AI.Sentinel.Tests.csproj, once per TargetFramework Condition. Renovate cannot see the Condition, so it rewrites both lines to the same version and pushes the net10.0-only package onto net8.0 (NU1202). Keep the net8.0 line inside 8.x; the net10.0 line updates normally. The pin rule above has the same blind spot and ignores allowedVersions, so the first pin PR rewrote the 8.0.33 line to [10.0.14] and broke restore on net8.0 again; rangeStrategy replace keeps this line out of the pin. The csproj keeps the exact 8.0.33 and Renovate still moves it within 8.x. Lift this when the two references can be told apart, for example by one central version per target framework.

ZeroAlloc.Serialisation.SystemTextJson requires a ZeroAlloc.Serialisation at least as new as itself, and AI.Sentinel.Tests references both directly. The shared preset groups only ZeroAlloc.Serialisation + generator, so the SystemTextJson bump arrived alone in #288, raised that floor past the pinned ZeroAlloc.Serialisation and broke restore with NU1605. Keep the family in one group so it always moves together.
